title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities crosses spatial and taxonomic boundaries without practical homogenization
frozen_core_claims: Recent-rain conditions are associated with expansion of the behaviourally realized acoustic community across active spatial footprint, local alpha richness and route gamma richness in NAAMP.
Taxonomic depth within already-active acoustic units is directionally consistent across independent North American NAAMP stops and Australian FrogID recordings.

The frozen Australian primary continuous-depth coefficient is -0.08176 species per 1 SD increasing log dry-spell exposure, with 95% CI -0.09816 to -0.06535; recorder-clustered and within-ERA5-cell sensitivities are also fully negative.
The North American exact species x stop incidence allocation strongly rejects a magnitude-matched uniform-activation null under kappa 1, 2 and 5.
Under the primary kappa=2 null, boundary crossing is 92.0 percent observed versus an 80.9 percent null mean and a 74.2-87.4 percent 95 percent null interval.
Pairwise Sorensen differentiation in NAAMP is practically equivalent to zero change within the fixed post hoc +/-0.025 slope margin in both the primary and exact-consecutive-year samples.
frozen_interpretation: Hierarchical generality: rainfall-associated taxonomic deepening within already-active acoustic units is cross-continentally consistent across North American and Australian monitoring systems; where fixed North American spatial matrices are available, additional participation is also more boundary-biased than uniform amplification predicts without practical local homogenization.
frozen_negative_boundaries: No worldwide or universal rainfall-response claim.
No pooled North America-Australia effect size and no equality-of-effect-size claim.
No claim that FrogID replicates the fixed ten-stop species x stop geometry.
No claim of identical mechanism across continents.
No rainfall causality, occupancy, abundance, colonization, extinction or demographic-recruitment claim.
Activation geometry remains falsified as a rainfall-specific species trait.
No claim of exact beta-diversity invariance or equivalence of every beta metric.
